source: Hand-curated Nov 15 2026 (valley ring plus far ring to about 330 mi). Names and coordinates from Google Places; hours, closures and seasons checked against venue sites, Visit Solvang, county and state park pages. Verify before booking. distMi is approximate road miles from Solvang Village Square.

items.name: Old Mission Santa Inés
items.note: 1804 mission, the 19th of California's 21, with a church, museum and gardens. Still an active parish; self-guided tours 9 to 4:30.
items.seasonNote: Closed New Year's Day, Easter, July 4, Thanksgiving and Christmas.

items.name: Elverhøj Museum of History & Art
items.note: The best short answer to why a Danish town is in California: local history, Danish-American stories and an art gallery.
items.seasonNote: Open Thu to Mon 11 to 5, closed Tue and Wed. Closed Thanksgiving, Dec 24, 25, 31 and Jan 1. Wiinblad exhibit through Jan 10, 2027.

items.name: Hans Christian Andersen Museum
items.note: Small museum above The Book Loft on Mission Drive about the fairy-tale author. Open daily 10 to 5; admission not posted.

items.name: Solvang Viking Museum
items.note: California's only Viking museum, with two reproduction ships, weapons and rune stones. Open daily. Coordinates approximate (1660 Copenhagen Dr).

items.name: Solvang Windmills & Village Walk
items.note: The postcard stop on Copenhagen Drive: windmills, shops and bakeries. Touristy but free and walkable.

items.name: Solvang Julefest (lights, parade, light and music show)
items.note: Month-long Danish Christmas: nightly light and music shows in Solvang Park, tree lighting Dec 4 at 5:30pm, parade Dec 5 at 11am.
items.seasonNote: Runs Nov 27, 2026 to Jan 3, 2027. Light shows on the hour 5 to 9pm.

items.name: Hans Christian Andersen Park
items.note: Playground, shaded trails and the Little Mermaid statue just north of the village.

items.name: Solvang Trolley & Carriage Tours
items.note: Narrated horse-drawn trolley ride around the village behind Belgian draft horses.

items.name: OstrichLand USA
items.note: Feed 80-plus ostriches and 70 emus from a bowl on a 32-acre farm. Open daily 9 to 6.
items.seasonNote: Emu eggs in winter, ostrich eggs in spring and summer.

items.name: Nojoqui Falls Park
items.note: Easy, shaded 0.65-mile walk to a seasonal waterfall of roughly 80 feet, plus picnic lawns and a playground.
items.seasonNote: Falls run best after winter rain (Dec to Apr) and shrink to a trickle in summer and fall.

items.name: Santa Ynez Chumash Museum & Cultural Center
items.note: The Santa Ynez Band of Chumash tell their own story here (opened 2025). Buy tickets online ahead.
items.seasonNote: Open Thu to Sun 10 to 5; closed Mon to Wed.

items.name: Santa Ynez Valley Historical Museum & Carriage House
items.note: Stagecoaches and horse-drawn carriages plus regional saddlery in the town of Santa Ynez. Coordinates approximate (3596 Sagunto St).
items.seasonNote: Open Wed to Sat noon to 4 only.

items.name: Cachuma Lake Recreation Area
items.note: Reservoir about 12 miles east on Hwy 154 with boat and kayak rentals, a nature center and trails. No swimming (drinking water).
items.seasonNote: Naturalist lake cruises out of service until further notice (Oct 2026). Day use $10 a car, closed Christmas.

items.name: Figueroa Mountain Road & wildflower fields
items.note: Winding climb from Los Olivos into Los Padres National Forest; poppies and lupine in spring, big valley views year-round.
items.seasonNote: Wildflowers usually Feb to Apr. Storms and snow can close the road; fire restrictions were in force in Oct 2026. Check Los Padres alerts.

items.name: La Purísima Mission State Historic Park
items.note: California's most completely restored mission: gardens, a church, and corrals with burros and longhorns. $6 a car.
items.seasonNote: Buildings 9 to 4; tours Wed to Sun at 1pm (Sat also 11am). Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day.

items.name: Alma Rosa Winery tasting room (Solvang)
items.note: Tasting room in the village for a Santa Rita Hills producer; an easy first tasting on foot.

items.name: Rideau Vineyard
items.note: Winery and vineyard tasting room on Alamo Pintado Road toward Los Olivos.

items.name: Brave & Maiden Estate
items.note: Estate winery and farm on N Refugio Road in Santa Ynez.

items.name: Roblar Winery & Vineyards
items.note: Winery and vineyard on Roblar Avenue north of Santa Ynez.

items.name: Gainey Vineyard
items.note: Estate winery and tasting room on Hwy 246 east of Santa Ynez.

items.name: peasants FEAST
items.note: Michelin Bib Gourmand farm-driven comfort food: Solvang Hot Chicken, mushroom tacos, beet grilled cheese. No reservations.
items.seasonNote: Open Wed to Sun 11 to 6; closed Mon and Tue.

items.name: Mad & Vin at The Landsby
items.note: Wine-country New American with vegetarian and vegan options; breakfast (7:30 to 11) and dinner (5 to 10).

items.name: Whiskey 'N Rye Smokehouse
items.note: Smokehouse barbecue on Atterdag Road. Closed Tuesdays.
items.seasonNote: Closed Tuesdays.

items.name: Solvang Restaurant
items.note: Danish meatballs and waffles; busy and no online reservations.

items.name: KANOK Thai Cuisine
items.note: Thai kitchen on Alisal Road, a break from the Danish menus.

items.name: The Gathering Table
items.note: Asian-fusion dining room on Mission Drive, dinner only (5 to 9).

items.name: Café Dolce
items.note: Coffee, breakfast, panini and acai bowls with vegan options; open early and late.

items.name: brekkies by chomp
items.note: Brunch spot on Mission Drive.

items.name: Birkholm's Bakery & Cafe
items.note: Bakery, coffee and sandwiches on Alisal Road.

items.name: Olsen's Danish Village Bakery
items.note: Danish pastries and aebleskiver, a Solvang ritual.

items.name: Mortensen's Danish Bakery
items.note: Danish bakery on Mission Drive.

items.name: Solvang Bakery
items.note: Pastries and cakes on Alisal Road.

items.name: The Baker's Table
items.note: Bakery and cafe on Sagunto Street in Santa Ynez.

items.name: S.Y. Kitchen
items.note: Italian kitchen in Santa Ynez.

items.name: Brothers Restaurant at the Red Barn
items.note: Special-occasion American dining in Santa Ynez.

items.name: Los Olivos Café
items.note: California wine-country cafe on Grand Avenue with a patio and a big local wine list.

items.name: Lucky Penny
items.note: Casual pizza in Los Olivos.

items.name: Vega Vineyard and Farm
items.note: Farm, winery and restaurant in Buellton, open 11 to 5 (lunch).

items.name: Leo's Cafe
items.note: Local breakfast and lunch favorite, open 8 to 2, closed Sundays.
items.seasonNote: Closed Sundays.

items.name: Belgian Cafe
items.note: Waffles and sandwiches in the village, open 7 to 3.

items.name: Craft House at Corque
items.note: Hotel bar and grill in the village; breakfast, then dinner from 3:30.

items.name: Santa Ynez Valley Breakfast
items.note: Breakfast and lunch, open 6:30 to 1.

items.name: Feather & Fire
items.note: Casual American in Buellton, closed Mondays.
items.seasonNote: Closed Mondays.

items.name: The Tavern at Zaca Creek
items.note: Wine bar and kitchen near Buellton, open 4 to 8, closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

items.name: PONY Cocktails + Kitchen
items.note: Californian kitchen in Santa Ynez, breakfast, lunch and dinner.

items.name: Nella Kitchen & Bar
items.note: Los Olivos Italian, open 11:30 to 8:45.

items.name: Bar Le Côte
items.note: Coastal seafood in Los Olivos, evenings only; closed Mon, Tue and Sat.
items.seasonNote: Closed Monday, Tuesday and Saturday.

items.name: The Tavern at the Los Olivos Hotel
items.note: Californian tavern in Los Olivos, breakfast, lunch and dinner.

items.name: Stearns Wharf
items.note: Santa Barbara's 1872 pier: seafood counters, shops and sea views. The classic stop.

items.name: Funk Zone
items.note: Old warehouses turned tasting rooms, breweries, murals and small restaurants a block from the beach.

items.name: Old Mission Santa Barbara
items.note: The 'Queen of the Missions' above the city. Check hours before you go.

items.name: Santa Barbara Botanic Garden
items.note: California native plants on trails above the mission. Quiet on weekdays.

items.name: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History
items.note: Whale skeleton, Chumash exhibits and a butterfly pavilion that is best in warm months. Open daily 10 to 5.
items.seasonNote: Butterfly pavilion is better in warm months.

items.name: Shalhoob's Funk Zone
items.note: Casual Funk Zone spot. Confirm hours.

items.name: The Lark
items.note: Shared-plate dining in the Funk Zone. Reserve ahead.

items.name: Loquita
items.note: Spanish tapas on State Street. Reserve ahead.

items.name: Brass Bear Brewing
items.note: Funk Zone brewery.

items.name: Bart's Books (Ojai)
items.note: Famously half-outdoor used bookstore. Small, easy and very Ojai.

items.name: Ojai Valley Downtown & Arcade
items.note: Spanish revival arcade, shops, galleries and cafes. Stroll-and-sit town.

items.name: Ojai Rôtie
items.note: Rotisserie and salads in downtown Ojai.

items.name: The Dutchess
items.note: Downtown Ojai. Confirm hours.

items.name: The Nest
items.note: Downtown Ojai. Confirm hours.

items.name: Farmer and the Cook
items.note: Organic farm cafe outside Ojai, known for vegetarian plates.

items.name: Channel Islands NP Visitor Center (Ventura)
items.note: Free exhibits and a tower with telescopes for gray whales. Open 8:30 to 5 daily, closed Thanksgiving and Dec 25. Boats to the islands leave from Ventura Harbor.
items.seasonNote: Gray whales most common from mid-Dec to mid-March. Island boats can be cancelled by weather.

items.name: Guadalupe-Nipomo Dunes
items.note: Huge coastal dune system south of Pismo. Wide open and quiet midweek.

items.name: Pismo Monarch Butterfly Grove
items.note: Free eucalyptus grove where monarchs cluster. Counted 501 on Nov 9, 2026.
items.seasonNote: Late Oct to Feb; best late Nov to Jan.

items.name: SeaVenture Restaurant (Pismo)
items.note: Ocean-view seafood in Pismo. Confirm hours.

items.name: Oyster Loft (Pismo)
items.note: Seafood in Pismo. Confirm hours.

items.name: Marisol at The Cliffs
items.note: Cliffside dining at Shell Beach. Reserve ahead.

items.name: Morro Rock
items.note: The 576-foot volcanic plug at Morro Bay's harbor mouth. Free; sea otters in the bay.

items.name: The Hidden Kitchen (Cayucos)
items.note: Small-town Cayucos spot. Confirm hours.

items.name: Hearst Castle
items.note: Guided tours only, starting from the visitor center. Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day. Book ahead.
items.seasonNote: Closed Thanksgiving, Dec 25 and Jan 1; tours sell out on holiday weekends.

items.name: Elephant Seal Vista Point (Piedras Blancas)
items.note: Free daily viewing of elephant seals on the beach. Adult males arrive in November, births peak late January.
items.seasonNote: Best Dec to Mar; January is pupping season.

items.name: Tablas Creek Vineyard
items.note: Organic Rhone-style winery west of Paso. Tasting by reservation is a safe bet.

items.name: Eberle Winery
items.note: Long-running Paso winery with tours and cave tastings.

items.name: Tobin James Cellars
items.note: Casual Paso tasting room, a few miles east of town.

items.name: Sabor & Sazón
items.note: Paso Robles. Confirm hours.

items.name: The Alchemists' Garden
items.note: Paso Robles. Confirm hours.

items.name: Il Cortile
items.note: Italian in downtown Paso. Reserve ahead.

items.name: Carrizo Plain National Monument
items.note: Remote grassland valley and the San Andreas Fault. Almost empty. Best in a wet spring for wildflowers.
items.seasonNote: Wildflower bloom Mar to Apr in a good rain year. No services; bring fuel, food and water.

items.name: Pinnacles National Park
items.note: Volcanic spires, talus caves and California condors. Winter is the quiet season, with caves dripping.

items.name: Bixby Creek Bridge
items.note: The icon of Highway 1. Pullouts are closed with a parking ban, so view it from a legal stop.
items.seasonNote: Pullouts closed; no parking.

items.name: McWay Falls (Julia Pfeiffer Burns SP)
items.note: An 80-foot waterfall dropping onto the beach. Short, easy walk from the parking lot.
items.seasonNote: Highway 1 has one-way traffic control and some closures this month; check Caltrans before driving.

items.name: Big Creek Bridge
items.note: Quieter bridge viewpoint south of McWay.

items.name: Nepenthe
items.note: Cliff-top Big Sur restaurant with ocean views.

items.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
items.note: World-class aquarium on Cannery Row. Book timed tickets.

items.name: Carmel Mission Basilica
items.note: Restored mission with gardens. Closed Mon and Tue; Wed and Thu 10 to 3:30, Fri and Sat 10 to 4:30, Sun from 11:30.
items.seasonNote: Closed Monday and Tuesday.

items.name: Nora's Carmel
items.note: Carmel. Confirm hours.

items.name: Mission Ranch (Carmel)
items.note: Ranch-style restaurant and inn in Carmel.

items.name: Tunnel View (Yosemite)
items.note: The panorama of Yosemite Valley, El Capitan and Half Dome. Very busy.
items.seasonNote: Tioga Road and Glacier Point Road are closed for the season; the valley stays open but chains are often required Nov to Mar.

items.name: Yosemite Valley Floor Loop
items.note: Yosemite Falls, meadows and the Merced River. Chain controls are common in winter.

items.name: Mariposa Grove of Giant Sequoias
items.note: Giant sequoias in Yosemite's south end. The shuttle stops Dec 1; walk or ski in from the Welcome Plaza.
items.seasonNote: Road and shuttle close around Dec 1; reach on foot in winter.

items.name: General Sherman Tree (Sequoia NP)
items.note: The largest living tree by volume. Easy paved path.
items.seasonNote: Generals Highway usually closes early Jan to mid March; chains common in winter.

items.name: Moro Rock & Crescent Meadow
items.note: Granite dome stairway and a meadow loop. The road closes after snow.
items.seasonNote: Spur road closed after snowfall.

items.name: General Grant Tree (Kings Canyon NP)
items.note: The nation's Christmas tree, a short loop in Grant Grove, the easiest winter approach.

items.name: Joshua Tree NP Visitor Center
items.note: Start here for maps and trail conditions.

items.name: Hidden Valley Nature Trail
items.note: 1-mile loop through boulder-ringed valley. Best Oct to Apr.

items.name: Keys View
items.note: Overlook toward the Coachella Valley and San Andreas Fault.

items.name: Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve
items.note: Cliffside trails over the Pacific.

items.name: La Jolla Cove & Sea Lion Rookery
items.note: Sea lions and harbor seals right on the rocks. Smelly and charming.

items.name: Cabrillo National Monument
items.note: Point Loma lighthouse and tide pools. Gray whales pass from December.

items.name: Balboa Park Botanical Building
items.note: Open daily 10 to 4. Balboa Park museums are next door.

items.name: Georges at the Cove
items.note: Ocean-view dining above La Jolla Cove. Reserve ahead.

items.name: Duke's La Jolla
items.note: Hawaiian-style seafood at La Jolla Cove.

items.name: The Cottage La Jolla
items.note: Breakfast and lunch cafe in La Jolla, open 7:30 to 3 (Mon hours).

items.name: Cesarina (Point Loma)
items.note: Italian in Point Loma. Confirm hours.

items.name: Pure Thai & Vegetarian Cuisine
items.note: Thai with a big vegetarian menu in Point Loma.

items.name: Joshua Tree Saloon
items.note: Burgers and live music in Joshua Tree town.

items.name: Snake Bite Roadhouse (Yucca Valley)
items.note: Roadhouse in Yucca Valley, open evenings (Mon hours 4 to 11).

items.name: Pappy & Harriet's (Pioneertown)
items.note: Pioneertown barbecue and live music. A desert classic.

items.name: Mountain Oaks Cafe (Oakhurst)
items.note: Oakhurst, south entrance to Yosemite.

items.name: Charles Street Dinner House (Mariposa)
items.note: Mariposa dinner house on the way to Yosemite.

items.name: The Gateway Restaurant & Lodge (Three Rivers)
items.note: Riverside restaurant at the Sequoia entrance.

items.name: Sequoia Coffee & Kitchen (Three Rivers)
items.note: Coffee and kitchen in Three Rivers.
